reasoning: Both models agree the package is safe. The PKGBUILD is straightforward and standard - it downloads prebuilt binaries from Google's official storage (storage.googleapis.com), verifies checksums with b2sums, and installs them to /opt with standard symlinks and desktop entries. There's no malicious code execution during build/install, no eval/curl|bash, no dynamic URL fetching with execution, and no .install hooks. The additional JS files reviewed by qwen are part of the upstream application payload (node_modules) and are outside the scope of AUR injection detection per the threat model.
coverage_issues: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash reviewed only 2 files (PKGBUILD and desktop file), which is shallow. While it covered the critical PKGBUILD, it failed to check for .install scripts or other packaging-related files.

qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 reviewed 4 JS files from the application payload (node_modules/chrome-devtools-mcp), which are outside the scope of AUR injection detection. This is wasted effort on upstream application code rather than AUR packaging files.
learnings: File selection: Models should prioritize AUR packaging files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches, any scripts referenced by PKGBUILD functions) over application payload files (node_modules, src/). The threat model is about injection into AUR packaging, not the upstream application.
Coverage: Models should explicitly check for the existence of .install scripts and review them if present, even if not explicitly referenced in the PKGBUILD.

Prompt/assessment quality: The qwen model's detailed assessment of JS files from node_modules is accurate but irrelevant to the AUR injection threat model. The tool should guide models to focus exclusively on AUR packaging files and deprioritize or exclude application payload files from the selection pool.

Common failure mode: Models may waste effort reviewing application payload files instead of focusing on AUR packaging files. The tool should explicitly exclude application payload files (e.g., files under src/, node_modules/) from the file selection pool unless they are directly referenced by PKGBUILD functions.
